title: Code health: dead code, test gaps, duplicates, security
bridge: The code-health sweepers are like a cleanup sprint where many people point at problems and one person makes the change. Except: the pointers are tools and read-only agents that must prove each item. The single writer opens one small PR at a time.
intro: Four sweepers keep the codebase healthy: dead-code removers for FE and BE, a test-gap routine, a duplicates sweep and a security fixer. They share one shape: many readers find and prove, one writer changes. Most of these tickets are stretch work for weeks 10 to 12.

picture.caption: Finders propose, read-only judges prove, one writer opens one small PR.

at most 10 deletions, 5 tests or 1 merge per PR; one approval

p: Code-health work is mostly reading: which export is unused, which test is missing, which two functions are copies. Reading is where extra agents help. Writing is where they hurt, so one writer per change stays the rule.

Each sweeper has the same shape. A finder tool lists candidates. Read-only verifiers, often in parallel inside the VM, prove or drop each one. One writer session makes a small change, and the PR shows the proof.
The limits keep PRs reviewable: at most 10 deleted items, at most 5 new tests, one merge proposal a week. These are sizes of a PR, not limits on the agent's work.

callout.text: One writer per change. Verifiers and judges only read. A single session edits inside its charter's paths, and the false-heal rules hold it to its kind of change.

sections.h: FE dead code: knip finds, the verifier proves
p: knip is a tool that lists unused files, exports and dependencies in a JavaScript or TypeScript project. Add it to frontend as a pinned devDependency, with frontend/knip.json and the script "knip": "knip --reporter json". The FE guild reviews the config; run it by hand and tune the entries until false positives are rare.

knip only knows what its entry files reach. Next.js pages, stories, tests and scripts are entries, so their imports count as used. Dynamic imports and string references it cannot see; that is the verifier's job.

The fe-dead-code charter: frontend/**, never add_code, Sonnet 5.5 at medium, a lite Spot VM, daily at 04:17 Sunday to Thursday. Verifiers search for dynamic imports, string references, stories, e2e page objects and @r/libs exports. One writer deletes at most 10 proven items; verify, check-types and build must pass.
sections.because: A deletion is quick to review when each item comes with proof that nothing uses it.

sections.h: BE dead code: vulture, and how Django hides usage
p: vulture is a Python tool that reports unused code, each item with a confidence from 60 to 100. Unused backend code is harder to spot than FE code, because Django finds much of it by name.

Django hides usage in URLs, the admin, signals, Celery tasks and DRF hooks. Management commands, settings strings and the SDK hide it too. The verifier checks each one. The SDK and the public API are never touched.

Same flow as the FE remover: finders propose, the verifier proves, one writer deletes at most 10 items per PR, never add_code. Before done: the cloud unit tests and makemigrations --check. This one is stretch.
sections.because: Starting strict at confidence 80 means the verifier sees few, likely candidates, and we lower it only if it keeps up.

code.text:
# cloud/rhinoCloud/pyproject.toml: sketch of the [tool.vulture] block for the BE dead-code remover
[tool.vulture]
paths = ["rhinoCore", "rhinoTaskServices", "vulture_allowlist.py"]
exclude = ["*/migrations/*", "*/tests/*", "*/integration-tests/*", "*/rhino-containers/*"]
min_confidence = 80                 # start strict; lower it only if the verifier keeps up
ignore_decorators = [
    "@app.task",                    # Celery: app = Celery("rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tasks") in celery_tasks/app.py
    "@receiver",                    # Django signals
    "@admin.register",
    "@action",                      # DRF viewset extra actions
    "@property",
    "@*.setter",
]
ignore_names = [
    "Meta", "get_queryset", "get_serializer_class", "perform_create", "perform_update",
    "has_permission", "has_object_permission", "to_representation", "validate_*",
    "handle", "add_arguments",      # management commands
    "setUpTestData", "setUp", "tearDown",
]
# vulture_allowlist.py lists names used only by URL configs, settings strings or the published SDK.

sections.h: Test gaps: plant a bug, filter it, write the test
p: Coverage numbers do not say whether tests catch bugs. This weekly routine copies the roles of Meta's ACH, a published Meta system that writes tests with a model. There, engineers accepted 73% of the generated tests.
One agent plants a small, realistic bug, a mutant. One filters out fake mutants. One writes a test that catches it.

An equivalent mutant is a change that does not change behaviour, so no test can catch it; the filter drops those. A test is kept only if it fails on its planted bug and passes on clean code. At most 5 tests per PR.

It runs weekly per area, on recently changed code with low coverage. For FE, fcp already runs Stryker, a mutation-testing tool (npm run test:unit:mutation). Mutants it reports as surviving are a cheap extra source. The charter test-gaps may add tests only: any source change is a false heal.
sections.because: A test that fails on a planted bug proves it catches bugs, which a coverage number never does.

notes.text: Three roles; only the test writer edits files.
Lines changed in the last 30 days that no test covers: coverage report crossed with recent changes.

A mutant that does not build is useless.

The one writer: the add-tests skill, testing what the user or API caller sees.

sections.h: Duplicates: one merge proposal a week
p: Copies drift apart and double the bug fixing. But a refactor storm is not reviewable. This stretch sweep, the "abstraction police", proposes one merge a week.

Finders list near-duplicates: jscpd, a copy-paste detector, for frontend, pylint's duplicate-code check for cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore. Parallel read-only judges on Sonnet 5.5 at medium decide real duplication versus coincidence. Two pieces that change for different reasons stay apart.

One writer proposes one merge with no behaviour change. Proof: the existing tests and verify pass unchanged, and the PR shows the copies side by side. jscpd runs through the Nexus npm proxy or is baked into the image.
sections.because: Code that looks the same but changes for different reasons is not a duplicate. Merging it ties together two things that should move alone.

Rank by size times number of copies, and keep the top 10.
The judges run in parallel; each only reads.
Real duplication and the same reason to change. Coincidences stay apart.
One writer, one proposal: the biggest real duplicate.
Existing tests unchanged and green is the proof.

sections.h: Security fixer: bumps with a fixed version
p: Findings with a known fixed version are busywork for people, and they have audit deadlines. This stretch routine takes Dependabot alerts on fcp, and the Vanta findings that Vanil files in Jira, when a fixed version exists. It upgrades and proves the finding is gone.

Agents get no Wiz or Vanta credentials. Ask Ronen for the JQL, and whether Wiz findings reach Jira the same way. The fixer also says whether our code uses the vulnerable path; unreachable findings are still bumped, labelled low risk.

The fix reuses the upgrade fixers' pipeline or a base-image bump (lesson g5-6). Proof: the scanner, trivy fs on the lockfile or the image scan, before and after in the VM. Its owner is from DevOps, and the noise and ladder rules apply as for every routine.
sections.because: Only findings a version bump can fix go to the routine; everything else stays with people.

lab.title: Prove or drop (reading lab)

worked.do: knip reports an unused export, formatQuota, in frontend/src/lib/quota.ts. A verifier finds `await import("@r/lib/quota")` in a page. Keep or drop?
worked.see: Drop: a dynamic import uses it, and anything unsure is dropped.

worked.do: vulture reports a function send_digest decorated with @app.task at confidence 60. Does it reach the verifier?
worked.see: No: @app.task is in ignore_decorators, and 60 is below min_confidence 80.

worked.do: The dead-code writer's diff changes `import { a, b, unused } from "./x"` to `import { a, b } from "./x"`. False heal?
worked.see: No. An import line that only loses names is fine under add_code.

worked.do: The test writer's new test passes on clean code and also passes on its mutant. Kept?
worked.see: No. It must fail on its planted bug, so it does not prove anything.

worked.do: jscpd finds two 80-token copies: a date formatter in two features owned by different teams, which change for different reasons. Merge?
worked.see: No. sameReasonToChange is false, so the judges keep them apart.

worked.do: A Dependabot alert has no first_patched_version. What does fixableFindings do?
worked.see: Skips it. With no fixed release, it stays with people.

lab.faded: Write the proof table for a dead-code PR that deletes 3 exports. One row per item: where it was, the knip line, and the verifier's searches. The third row's searches are left to you.
lab.alone: Pick one real-looking pair of near-duplicate functions you have seen in a frontend codebase. Write the judge's answer for it: real duplication or not, same reason to change or not, and one line why. Then write the one-line merge proposal, or say why there is none.
lab.done: For each sweeper you can name the finder, what the verifier checks, what the single writer may change, and the PR size.

quiz.q: Why does the dead-code remover have never: add_code in its charter?

options.text: Because it may only delete; any new code means it is doing something other than removing dead code
options.why: The false-heal check rejects a deletions-only routine that adds code; shortened imports are fine.

options.text: Because new code needs a second approval
options.why: Approval is always exactly one; the rule is about the routine's kind of change.

options.text: Because knip cannot read new code
options.why: The rule is a charter rule, not a tool limit.

quiz.q: When does the test-gap routine keep a new test?

options.why: Coverage does not show a test catches bugs.

options.text: When it fails on its planted bug and passes on clean code
options.why: That proves the test catches a real kind of bug.

options.text: When the filter says the mutant is equivalent
options.why: Equivalent mutants are dropped; no test can catch them.

quiz.q: How many writers does the duplicates sweep use?

options.text: One per clone, in parallel, to save time
options.why: Parallel writers conflict; one writer per change.

options.text: One, proposing one merge a week; the judges only read
options.why: Many readers, one writer, one reviewable PR.

options.text: None; it only posts a report
options.why: One writer proposes one merge with proof.

words.plain: Code nothing uses any more; it slows people and agents and hides real usage.
A tool that lists unused files, exports and dependencies in a JS or TS project, from its entry files.
A Python tool that reports unused code with a confidence score.
A small planted bug used to check whether a test would catch it.
A change that does not change behaviour, so no test can catch it.
Two pieces of code that look alike; real duplication only if they change for the same reason.
